findings.detail: spec-coverage.sh flags SPEC.md:156's (no-test: ...) waiver on this chain's own R-13 (manual real-vault verification) as stale because the literal text 'R-13' appears in test files the plan scopes in (e.g. UITests/WorkspaceOpenStateUITests.swift:111, a doc comment dated 2026-08-26, predating this Step 5 segment). That comment references an UNRELATED R-13 from a different plan's own requirement numbering (each plan restarts its own R-01.. sequence) - it is not automated coverage of THIS chain's R-13, which remains genuinely human-only (real iCloud vault, cannot run unattended). Did not apply the tool's suggested remedy (deleting the no-test clause) because doing so would falsely claim R-13 is now test-covered when it is not.

waiver_decision.decision: Waive as false positive. SPEC.md's (no-test: ...) clause for R-13 stays untouched.
waiver_decision.rationale: Checker does a plan-wide substring match on the ID text across every test file the plan scopes in, with no awareness that requirement IDs restart at R-01 per plan. The 'R-13' hit is an ID collision with an unrelated plan's own numbering, not a real coverage gap.

findings.detail: Same mechanism: SPEC.md:159's (no-test: ...) waiver on this chain's R-16 (scripts/uitests.sh must pass, human-run only per CLAUDE.md) is flagged stale because 'R-16' appears in UITests/WorkspaceIntegrationUITests.swift:3, a doc-comment header dated 2026-08-24 from a DIFFERENT chain's plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-workspace-tasks-notes-integration.md, Task 10), which has its own, unrelated R-16. This chain's own R-16 (the human-run scripts/uitests.sh gate) has not been run by me, deliberately, and the waiver should NOT be deleted.

waiver_decision.decision: Waive as false positive. SPEC.md's (no-test: ...) clause for R-16 stays untouched.

CRITICAL.problem: board/document/contents stay populated with the previous board's data after select(.folder(f)); mutate/addNode/delete/move/resize/setColor/setText/connect/createFolder carry no guard on current.hasBoard, enforced only by view composition not by the model.
Re-derives the exact lowercased-lastPathComponent match rule WorkspaceBoardResolver.matches already centralizes, rather than calling the shared helper shipped in the same PR.

IMPORTANT.problem: try? on store.read(path) discards the real error, replaced with a flat "non leggibile" string. Pre-existing pattern in FolderFileOperations.swift, now duplicated into a second file rather than fixed.
Uses error.localizedDescription where every other error site touched by this chain interpolates the raw \(error), losing NSError domain/code detail on FileManager failures.

No wrapper type distinguishes a board-file path from a folder path (bare String everywhere); four independently-declared board-vs-folder discriminated unions (WorkspaceItemKind, WorkspaceTree.Node.Kind, WorkspaceSelection, PendingWorkspaceDelete) not convertible to one another.
OperationError declared identically twice (same 4 cases, same wording); RenamePlan/RenameOutcome are near-identical DTOs per file-kind rather than one shared shape.
draggingIDs/dragTranslation/resizingNodeID/etc. are plain var not private(set); doc comment admits the invariant lives in convention, not the type system.
board: String uses "" as a sentinel for "nothing open" rather than String?, duplicating what current: WorkspaceSelection? already carries — the two can drift (see CRITICAL finding 1).

SUGGESTIONS.problem: Silently returns on a PergamenumLink.canvas(...) miss with no recordProblem; pre-existing gap the chain touched (folder-derived path -> workspace.board) without fixing.
allBoards() ?? [] degrades conservative, boardNameIsAvailable ?? true degrades optimistic — asymmetric defaults on a nil store, worth a shared/explicit helper.
Computed on every successful rewrite but never consumed by VaultController.renameBoard (only .failures is read) — data computed and discarded.
Mixes pure static navigation-rule functions with six DI closures in one struct; a separate namespace would let the pure half be referenced/tested independently.
Carries a raw path, consistent with the missing-wrapper-type finding; natural first place to introduce a BoardPath wrapper before the pattern spreads further.

findings.positive_note: PendingWorkspaceRename/PendingWorkspaceDelete, WorkspaceSelection and WorkspaceBoardResolution were called out by type-design-analyzer as clean, well-encapsulated sealed unions with enforced invariants (.folder("") never produced, .unique/.ambiguous/.notFound covering every outcome with no nullable fallback) — the weaker spots are concentrated in the file-operations layer and the controller's mutation surface, not the new selection/resolution types themselves.
